author: Joost de Winter
claim_limitations: Complete 2026-11-11 rational centre-basis witness at 157, read exactly from the retained source file without its schema envelope, in the watched repository JoostdeWinter/square-packing, which jlevy/squares#958 names: a pinwheel the source derives from Samanyu-dev's public 109-square packing, by two cut-and-fill steps, the first giving its packing of 132. Finite construction feasibility only; the 250-digit contact solution, local optimum, KKT, rigidity, same-packing, novelty, priority and global optimality are not replayed here.

register.title: Joost de Winter's pinwheel packing of 157 squares at JoostdeWinter/square-packing 6617869, issue 958
register.headline: De Winter's pinwheel at 157 from Samanyu-dev's 109, the first below the grid's 13, by 6.70e-03
register.source_checks:
n157/README.md says all squares were optimized together with an interior-point solver (IPOPT) and the contact equations of the result then solved to 250 digits: all 2024 contact equations (a corner of one square on the edge line of another, or a corner on a wall) are satisfied to 1e-247 and all other gaps stay open, and the certificate's side is 1.4e-59 above that solution. It says non-negative contact forces in balance exist, the first-order condition for a local minimum, checked in floating point; that 297 perturbation trials, each re-optimized, found no smaller side; that local optimality has no formal proof; and that a search for a minimal polynomial of the side up to degree 16 found none. It says verify_exact.py, Python's standard library only, is the folder's exact checker. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.

The README says the Kaggle competition 'Squares in Squares' has a per-puzzle leaderboard that lists sides without packings, that the author has not seen its values at 157, and so an unpublished packing with a smaller side may exist.
register.credit:
Credit Joost de Winter, who reports a pinwheel, a central block of tilted squares with four arms surrounded by four blocks of axis-aligned squares (61 tilted, at four distinct angles between 24.0 and 27.6 degrees, and 96 upright), derived from the public 109-square packing of Samanyu-dev/squares_in_squares (best_fit_101_500.csv, side 10.949289581) in two steps, each cutting the packing along one horizontal and one vertical line, moving the parts about one unit apart, filling each gap with one layer of squares that continues the local lattice and re-optimizing every square; the first step gives his packing of 132. The README says credit for the pinwheel arrangement at n = 109 belongs to Samanyu-dev, whose README reports that packing as a result of its own stretch and quench chains; the issue makes no claim at 109 and names its own contribution as the growth steps and the optimization, so the packing at 157 is credited to de Winter after Samanyu-dev.

The README says the derivation, optimization, high-precision solution, rational certificate, checking and figure were produced with Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic) under the direction of Joost de Winter; 6617869 named the model in place of a491dad's 'Claude (Anthropic)'.
register.next_rung: Independently review the certificate (stage 4, a separate lane blind to this one): its mathematics, a clean-room exact checker with sharp controls, the identity against the grid and the construction the source states, mapped as an adversarial review, whose acceptance the verified lane and the house rule wait on. Then adopt it at 157 in place of the grid under the house rule, with both strong generators' regularization, measured against the new witness, and the flip of the new house in the same change.
